step_by_step_procedure: A circle is a closed plane curve of all points equidistant from center O.
Radius r is fixed compass distance from center to boundary.
Diameter d passes through center connecting opposite points.
sub_branches.example_problem: Radius r = 4.5 cm => Diameter d = 2 x 4.5 = 9.0 cm.

step_by_step_procedure: Mark a single center point O on paper.
Set compass to radius r_1 and draw inner circle.
Without moving needle from O, adjust compass span to r_2 and draw outer circle.
formulas_and_identities: Concentric Condition: Same Center O, Different Radii r_1 != r_2
sub_branches.example_problem: Draw concentric circles with r_1 = 3 cm and r_2 = 5 cm.

step_by_step_procedure: Set compass needle at 0 mark on ruler and align pencil leg to mark length L.
Transfer exact segment length without ruler tick parallax errors.
formulas_and_identities: Compass Span = Exact Physical Length L
sub_branches.example_problem: Transfer segment AB = 6.4 cm precisely using compass.

step_by_step_procedure: Place set-square 90° corner along baseline segment AB at vertex point.
Draw perpendicular ray along set-square vertical guide arm.
sub_branches.example_problem: Construct perpendicular ray at vertex A of base segment AB = 6 cm.

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1: Draw base line segment AB = length l.
Step 2: Construct perpendicular rays at A and B using set-square.
Step 3: Mark width w along rays to locate vertices D and C.
Step 4: Join C and D to complete rectangle ABCD.
formulas_and_identities: Rectangle Construction: 4 x 90° corners, opposite equal sides
sub_branches.example_problem: Construct rectangle with length 6 cm and width 4 cm.

sub_branches.concept_or_rule: Inscribing Regular Hexagon using Radius Arcs
step_by_step_procedure: Keep compass opening locked at radius r.
Starting at any point on boundary, step consecutive r-length arcs around circle.
Join the 6 arc intersection points to form a regular hexagon.
sub_branches.example_problem: Inscribe regular hexagon in circle of radius 4 cm. Side length = 4 cm.
